code.why: Raised only when the SQL engine (src/engine/sql.ts) throws something other than MySQL's refusal (a SqlError): a defect of the engine itself, which every statement MySQL refuses answers as a SqlError instead.

The descriptor's credentialDoor: the World's runtime calls it at boot to issue the application's PLANETSCALE_DATABASE_URL. The life and the published examples make their passwords on the dashboard's Connect page and boot no application; the client cases (twin-world packages/twin-standard/src/clients/planetscale.ts) are the application that holds it.
The users door's refusal of a sign-up missing its email, password or organization name: the World's own door, called by the World with a whole sign-up; no customer of PlanetScale reaches it.
No dashboard form posts an unknown or absent action; this refusal protects against a hand-crafted malformed submission.

Answers a native-wire sign-in whose user's passwords all have a secret this World can no longer derive again (its seed for them changed after they were made, the case the credential door's own re-derivation guards, api/src/semantics/doors.ts). Every password the dashboard makes in a World derives again, so neither the life nor the published examples can make one; the refusal names it rather than calling the password wrong.
